raw_response:
Five useful references for this immutable, ordered constant-set design:

1. [Java 5 enum types](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/1.5.0/docs/guide/language/enums.html) supply named values separated from integers, declaration-order iteration, and comparison restricted to the same enumeration. The [Enum API](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/1.5.0/docs/api/java/lang/Enum.html) also prevents cloning. A Python adaptation needs runtime domain checks and freezing, and additional fields must not undermine immutability. The versioned documentation was opened; its precise historical publication date remains unverified in this run.

2. [Haskell 98 derived instances](https://www.haskell.org/onlinereport/derived.html) offer a useful separation of capabilities: nullary constructors provide distinct named values, while selected Eq, Ord, Enum and Bounded instances provide comparison and traversal without automatically supplying arithmetic. Python would need runtime checks in place of Haskell's static separation. Explicit conversions and successor/predecessor boundary errors need deliberate policy. The linked report is dated December 2002.

3. [Apache Commons Lang 2.1 Enum](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-lang/javadocs/api-2.1/org/apache/commons/lang/enums/Enum.html) is a library-based model for named constants, lookup, iteration and canonical deserialization. Iteration follows creation order but comparison defaults to alphabetical order; adapting it requires aligning those orders and closing subclass extension. The API records a 2005-04-14 source revision.

4. [Ada 95 enumeration types](https://www.adaic.org/resources/add_content/standards/95aarm/AARM_HTML/AA-3-5-1.html) define a finite domain of distinct named values with declaration-position ordering. The [scalar-type rules](https://www.adaic.org/resources/add_content/standards/95aarm/AARM_HTML/AA-3-5.html) distinguish enumeration from numeric types and define bounds and successor/predecessor operations. These semantics transfer to Python, but an immutable namespace and runtime domain checks still need implementation. The opened manual identifies the 1995 standard with its 2000 corrigendum.

5. [Python Immutable Enumerations Using Duck Punching](https://code.activestate.com/recipes/578294-python-immutable-enumerations-using-duck-punching/) is later evidence for a partial mechanism: property descriptors reject assignment and deletion of existing names. It returns raw values and permits unrelated attributes, so it does not meet the full isolation, ordering and immutability requirements. Its original-site metadata dates creation to 2012-10-18, after the cutoff.

These are design references and implementation starting points, not claims of deployment or demonstrated usefulness. The public unauthenticated grep.app request was inaccessible; public OpenJDK code was inspected through a code-through-web fallback, not native code-search success. Current OpenJDK source was not treated as pre-cutoff evidence. A general search exposed excluded proposal snippets and there was recognized proposal-related memory; both are recorded as exposures, and no proposal page was opened.
limitations: The general Python query returned excluded proposal-copy snippets and discussion snippets despite exclusion terms; these exposures and recognized memory are recorded, so this is not a fully unexposed run.

The unauthenticated grep.app API attempt was inaccessible through the available web tool. Code-through-web search and a public OpenJDK source read were used as fallback; no native code-search success is claimed.
Opened-page budget conservatively counts every open, click and targeted find attempt, including repeats, failed fetches and redirects; it is not a count of unique URLs.

The Java 5 version-specific pages were available, but attempted historical specification URLs redirected to current JDK 27 documentation. Java candidate chronology is therefore marked unknown; live OpenJDK source is also undated evidence.
The Python recipe body was opened; its exact creation date was obtained from original-site search metadata because subsequent date-section reads returned HTTP 502.
Cross-language mechanisms need translation into Python and were not implemented, executed or tested. The later Python recipe is a partial immutability component, not a complete solution.
